observations: With equal random selection of fair and two-headed coins, three heads raised the displayed probability from fifty through sixty-seven and eighty to eighty-nine percent.
One thousand pulls produced 578 HHH sequences, of which 505 were two-headed, displayed as 87 percent.
A second drawn coin produced tails within three flips and probability zero; prior batch evidence remained labeled.
Reveal explains odds doubling from one-to-one to eight-to-one, eight of nine probability, and the decisive tails countercase.

complexity.conceptualDemand: Update relative hypothesis support rather than raw head frequency.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Flip, triple flip, batch and new-coin controls.

whyCool: Each head doubles the odds without proving the coin's identity, while one tail can settle it.
caveat: Exactly two ideal coin hypotheses and equal selection; simulated batch is not empirical coin data.
effort: Prediction, three-head trajectory, thousand-pull batch, second coin with tails, screenshot and reveal.
